curriculum.subject: English Language Activities
curriculum.subStrand: Yes/ No questions (with can, may, will)
curriculum.outcomeText: respond to Yes/No questions using can, may and will, for clarity in communication

interactions.prompt: Can a bird fly? Choose a clear answer.
interactions.feedback: Yes! We answer a can question with can.
interactions.retryHint: Repeat the helping word used in the question.

interactions.prompt: May I borrow your pencil? You agree. What do you say?
interactions.feedback: Great! “Yes, you may” clearly gives permission.
interactions.retryHint: The question asks for permission using may.

interactions.prompt: Match each question to its clear answer.
interactions.tapAlternative: Tap a question, then tap the answer with the same helping word.
interactions.feedback: Well done! Each answer matches its question word.
interactions.retryHint: Listen for can, may, or will in each question.

interactions.prompt: Will Asha come today? She cannot come. Which answer is clear?
interactions.feedback: Correct! The answer clearly responds to will.
interactions.retryHint: Use will in the answer because will is in the question.

interactions.prompt: Sort the answers by the question word they answer.
interactions.tapAlternative: Tap an answer, then tap can, may, or will.
interactions.feedback: Excellent! You found the helping word inside every answer.
interactions.retryHint: Say each answer and listen for can, may, or will.

interactions.prompt: Your friend asks, “Can you play now, or will you play later?” You cannot play now but agree to play later. Which response is clearest?
choices: No, I cannot play now, but yes, I will play later.
interactions.answer: No, I cannot play now, but yes, I will play later.
interactions.feedback: Fantastic! You answered both parts clearly with can and will.
interactions.retryHint: The answer needs one part about ability now and one part about the future.
